💾 Protect your work — Save, Back up & Restore
Your work is saved automatically in your browser as you edit. Because it lives in this browser, use the tools below to write your .filter to disk and keep copies safe:
• Save — write the game .filter to your Path of Exile 2 folder, optionally to several folders at once.
• Back up — keep a full copy of your whole editor state, on disk if you like.
• Restore — load any backup back in one click, or move your filter to another computer.

💾 Save, Back up & Restore
1Save — write the .filter to disk. go
2Back up — save a full copy you can recover from. go
3Restore — load a backup back in one click. go
1Save — your game-ready .filter

Your work auto-saves in the browser as you edit. Export / Quick-Save writes the .filter the game reads into your Path of Exile 2 folder — click it whenever you want the game to see your changes.

📍 Multi-Location Save
Add up to 4 folders (cloud, game folder, external drive…) and every save writes to all of them. Each has a dropdown for what to save there.
For the game folder (...\My Games\Path of Exile 2) choose "Just the .filter" — the game only reads that file.
The dropdown options:
Just the .filter — the raw file the game reads.
.filter + .meta.json — plus its sidecar (keeps tier config for re-import).
Everything (recommended for a cloud folder) — a full copy of your working session, always current.
2Back up — a full copy you can recover from

A backup captures everything — rules, sections, tiers, sounds, settings — not just the .filter. MirrorFilter backs up automatically before anything risky, and can keep timestamped copies in a folder you control.

Back up now saves both at once: an in-browser restore point (last 8 kept) and, if disk backup is on, a timestamped file in your folder. Also happens on every Quick-Save and every 5 minutes.
3Restore — load a backup back

Pick a saved backup and load it. Your current state is backed up first, so it's always reversible.

From your backup folder? Backups are mirrorfilter-backup-DATE_TIME.json — newest = latest date. (The .filter/.meta.json there are the game files, not full backups — load a .filter via Import at the top.)
⚡ Core Setup
⚡ Tier System & Auto-Tier Configuration — click to expand/collapse ▶
⚡ Auto-Tier — sorts BaseTypes into tiers by live price when you click it:

Enable on a rule by checking Tier Sort Target in the Editor.
All rules with Tier Sort Target checked in the same section form a sort group. When Auto-Tier runs, it collects every BaseType across all rules in that group, looks up each item's price (see the price-source breakdown below), then redistributes them: each BaseType goes into the rule whose tier threshold its price meets. BaseTypes that fall below the lowest threshold are removed from all rules. Visuals are never touched — only the BaseType lists change.

Example: You have 5 rules in "Currency": S-Tier, A-Tier, B-Tier, C-Tier, D-Tier — all with Tier Sort Target ✓. You add Divine Orb, Exalted Orb, Chaos Orb, Orb of Alteration etc. across them. Click ⚡ Auto-Tier — prices are fetched, and each item is moved to the correct tier rule automatically. A Chaos Orb that was in B-Tier yesterday may move to C-Tier today.

⚠ Rules stay in their sections always. Auto-Tier never moves a rule from Currency to Uniques or anywhere else.

Requires an internet connection. Prices are cached server-side for 5 minutes per league — clicking Auto-Tier again sooner reuses the cached numbers instantly; after 5 minutes, the next click fetches fresh prices.
Where Prices Come From
Three sources are tried in order, each one only filling in items the ones before it didn't have — nothing is ever overwritten by a later source:

1 poe.ninja — primary, and now matched exactly to poe.ninja's own official API documentation. Covers Currency, Runes, Soul Cores, Essences, Fragments, Catalysts, Omens, Liquid Emotions, Expedition, Abyss, Uncut Gems, Lineage Support Gems, Idols, and Verisium — plus Tablets (both Precursor and Unique), Relics, Weapons, Armours, Accessories, Flasks, Charms, and Jewels via its separate per-item pricing data.
2 poe2scout — supplemental. Currently returning HTTP 404 on every attempt (broke during their Cloudflare migration), but still tried, since its original bulk endpoint covers uniques/jewels/idols/gear poe.ninja doesn't — it'll automatically start contributing again the moment it recovers.
3 poe2db.tw — last resort. A live economy tracker with no public API, so this parses its pages directly for whatever the first two still missed — mainly Runes/Soul Cores/Essences/Fragments as a backup for poe.ninja's own coverage of those.
Every attempt — success or failure, from all three sources — is written to UserData\economy_debug.log if you ever need to see exactly what happened on a given run.
Tier Configuration
Tiers are checked highest-threshold first. Items with chaos value ≥ the threshold get that tier. The lowest tier (0 threshold) is the catch-all.

🎨 Price Color Gradient
Controls how prices are colored on BaseType chips and the price panel — dull for the cheapest item, bright vivid for the priciest. Pick a color family below, and adjust where the midpoint sits.
More dull More bright
Bias: 1.00 (1.00 = neutral)
🔲 Estimated Price Border
A generic BaseType (e.g. bare "Shortsword" with no specific unique named) can't be priced directly — Auto-Tier instead estimates it using the highest-priced specific unique currently known to use that base, and marks the price with a border so it reads as an estimate rather than a direct fetch. Pick which sections should actually show that border — defaults to sections with "Unique" in the name, since that's where this situation comes up; unchecked sections show the estimated price with no visual marker at all.

🔍 Filter Drift Check — catch rules that moved to the wrong section ▶
This is a report, not a backup — it never changes or restores your filter. Once your filter is organized the way you like, save a reference snapshot of it here. Later, the drift check compares your current rules against that reference and flags any that have moved to a different section since (e.g. a rule that ended up under the wrong heading). For recovering lost work or undoing changes, use Saving Your Work → ② Back up instead — that's the backup/restore system.

🔊 Custom Alert Sounds & Configurations — click to expand/collapse ▶
Add .mp3, .wav, or .ogg sound file paths from your PC. They appear in the Alert Sound dropdown alongside the 16 default game sounds. Exports as CustomAlertSound "path" 300. 🎯 Bulk Visual Assign — click to expand/collapse ▶
Set a Minimap Icon and/or Beam Effect Color on many rules across many sections at once. This overwrites whatever a rule already has — nothing is merged or preserved. Every Apply asks for confirmation first and comes with an Undo button on the toast afterward; there's also a separate Clear button below to reset everything to blank on demand.
Step 1 — Pick your sections
Each row below has two checkboxes: the left one picks a section as a target for Step 3. The right one, Never, marks a section you'll never want an icon/beam on at all (e.g. plain Magic/Normal item sections) — it strikes the row through, disables its target checkbox, and sorts it to the very bottom so it stops cluttering the list. Sections you've already applied to are tracked automatically and shown in green, sorted just above the Never ones — a quick way to see what's left to do.
Step 2 — Pick a mode
For each rule: sets Minimap Icon Color and Beam Effect Color to whichever of the 11 palette colors is closest to that rule's own background color — no manual color picking needed, and every rule in a tiered set (A/B/C/D/E/etc.) naturally ends up matching, since they usually already share a similar background hue. Minimap Icon Size is set automatically by tier rank: your highest tier (e.g. A) gets Largest, the next two get Medium, everything else (including your Unpriced Catch-All) gets Small — based on your actual configured tier order, not hardcoded letters.
Shape (same for every rule):
Minimap Icon Color and Minimap Icon Size are automatic per rule, as described above — not manually chosen here.

📋 Custom Paste Include/Exclude Lists — click to expand/collapse ▶
When bulk-pasting a list from a website table (e.g. poe.ninja) into a BaseType/Class/mod picker, some text gets automatically recognized as noise and skipped — numbers, prices, percentages, UI labels like "wiki" or "Trade". These two lists let you correct that yourself, without needing a code update:
🚫 Exclude List
If something slips through and gets added as a fake item, add the exact text here — it'll be treated as noise on every future paste, exact match, case-insensitive.
✅ Include List
The opposite case: if a real item name ever gets wrongly treated as noise and skipped (e.g. it happens to contain a number, or looks like one of the built-in patterns), add its exact text here — it'll always be recognized as a real item on every future paste, bypassing the normal noise checks entirely.

🎮 Game Mode
Affects BaseTypes, Classes, Conditions, and HasExplicitMods — each is suggested per game. The built-in Conditions are split from GGG's own official reference (6 are PoE2-only: AlwaysShow, HasVaalUniqueMod, IsVaalUnique, TwiceCorrupted, UnidentifiedItemTier, WaystoneTier; PoE1-only: HasInfluence, HasEaterOfWorldsImplicit, HasSearingExarchImplicit, plus SocketType since PoE2 has no socket colors). HasExplicitMods have no official machine-readable master list to split from, so instead each custom mod you add carries its own PoE1 / PoE2 / Both tag (set it when you add it, or change it later in the Custom HasExplicitMods list) — when the tool is set to one game, only that game's mods plus "Both" are suggested. This only affects suggestions; anything already in your rules keeps working exactly as before regardless of this setting, and mods added before this update default to "Both" so nothing disappears.
⚠ PoE1 Classes are populated, but PoE1 BaseTypes aren't built into the suggestion list yet — switching to "PoE1 Only" will show an empty BaseType picker until that data is added in a future update. Custom BaseTypes you add yourself below work in any mode.
🔧 Custom Conditions
Add custom condition keys to the inline condition picker (click + Add Condition on a rule). All standard PoE2 conditions are already built in. Use this for new conditions added in future patches — no app update needed.
📦 Custom BaseTypes
Add BaseType values as quick-pick suggestions when adding a BaseType condition in the Editor. Use this for new PoE1/PoE2 item base types not yet in the built-in list.
🏷 Custom Classes
Add Class values as quick-pick suggestions when adding a Class condition in the Editor. Use this for new item classes added in future patches.
🔮 Custom HasExplicitMods
Add HasExplicitMod values as quick-pick suggestions when adding a HasExplicitMod condition in the Editor. These could previously only be added via paste-import — this is the same list, now manageable by hand too.

🧹 Filter Cleanup Tools — click to expand/collapse ▶
Every tool below either only removes something *provably* empty/redundant (never touches conditions, visuals, or anything a rule actually matches on), or just reports findings without changing anything — you decide what, if anything, to do about those. Nothing here can silently change what your filter shows or hides in-game.
Safe — auto-fixes, always reversible via Undo where applicable
e.g. a rule listing "Divine Orb" twice by accident
only removes sections with nothing in them at all, at any depth
a tier rule left enabled with nothing in it can accidentally catch items it was never meant to
older sessions may have leftover tier values on rules that were never meant to be tier-sorted — actual Tier Sort Target rules are left completely alone
Find & Replace in Rule/Section Names — only ever touches display names/labels, never conditions, visuals, or matching logic
→
Find & Remove Text in Rule/Section Names — removes the matched text from names, same as Find & Replace with a blank replacement
Report only — shows findings, you decide what to do
▶ Sections to include in the two BaseType duplicate checks below
same BaseType in two rules in the same section — usually accidental, but not deleted for you
same BaseType in two different sections — often fine on purpose, shown so you can judge for yourself
same section + action + conditions — could be intentional, so nothing is deleted for you

🗑️ Removed BaseTypes/Classes/Mods Log — click to expand/collapse ▶
Every time you click ✕ on a single BaseType, Class, or mod inside a rule's conditions, it gets logged here — a running record of what you've removed, so you can review the batch later and tell me which ones (if any) should be purged from MirrorFilter's internal BaseType/Class database entirely, e.g. if the game is rejecting them as PoE1-only leftovers. Nothing here is ever removed from the database automatically — this is just a record for you to review.
🔍 Missing Values Tracker — click to expand/collapse ▶

When you paste a list of Classes, BaseTypes, or HasExplicitMods from another .filter or from a website table (poe.ninja, poe2scout, etc) — "Item One" "Item Two" (quoted), Item One, Item Two (comma-separated), Item One ♦ Item Two (diamond-separated — the format some sites' formatted lists copy as), or one per line — every item gets added to your rule right away. Anything that doesn't match MirrorFilter's built-in suggestion list is added too, as a new custom value, and ALSO recorded here automatically so you can review the gaps later and hand them back for the tool's built-in lists to be properly updated. Nothing sits blocked waiting on that review — it's a convenience log, not a gate.

Pasting straight from a price-tracking site's table (name plus price, level, DPS, 7-day trend, etc all copied together) works too — MirrorFilter looks for a recognized item name anywhere in each line, junk before or after included, and keeps just the name.

Click ✕ next to any single value to remove just that one — handy once you've reported it and don't need it cluttering the list anymore. "Clear" wipes the whole list at once. "Check for Added Items" doesn't remove anything by itself — it just pre-checks (shown in green) whatever it finds already in the tool, so you can review and uncheck anything first. Once you've got the right items checked: Remove Checked from Checklist only clears this tracker log, Remove Checked from Database only strikes them from the Custom database (they'll stay logged here), and Remove Checked from Both does both at once.

⚡ Auto-Tier — Full Explanation

⚡ Auto-Tier fetches live prices and sorts BaseTypes into tiers:

Check Tier Sort Target on rules in the Editor. Rules with this checked in the same section form a sort group. Auto-Tier collects all BaseTypes across the group, prices them via poe.ninja, then redistributes each one into the rule whose tier threshold matches its price. BaseTypes below the lowest threshold are removed. Visuals never change.

Tier thresholds are configurable in Resources → Tier System.

Rules always stay in their sections. Auto-Tier never moves a rule between sections.
